title: Fix intern-reset large-elim and def-codomain Prop-ctor PI
body:

Aggregator: `/tmp/mathlib_full.ndjson` (`lake env lean4export Mathlib`, 5.3GB, Lean 4.29.1, mathlib `v4.29.1` / `5e932f9`). `KIOTA_NBE` unset. `CONV_DEPTH` 8192. No pin, no name special-case, no HasSize skip shipped, no HPow/Pow eta shipped.

Hunt loader (not kernel, binary copied out, tree restored clean): `KIOTA_MIN_DECL=226030` (intern_clear still runs on skipped prefix; `check_inductive_group` skipped below MIN), `KIOTA_SKIP_DECLS` as listed below.

| --- | --- |
| Leftover | `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsHomLift` |
| Decl# | last `check_last` `#62400` on the HomLift-module export (inductive blocks are not counted); then `check_inductive_group` |
| Error class | recursor allows large elimination out of a Prop-valued inductive that is not a subsingleton |

Lean elaborates this as Eq-shaped (`#print` motive `Sort u`, 5 params, 6 indices, 1 ctor / 3 fields). The 650KB decl-closure slice accepted. The 745MB whole-module export rejected after `intern_clear_if_large`.

Dump (`KIOTA_TRACE_ELIM0`): conclusion **does** contain bare `#2` / `#1` / `#0`. `found_ptr=false` because `ExprNode::eq` is intern pointer identity.

Fix: match de Bruijn **indices** on top-level conclusion args. Nested occurrences still do not count.

---

## Keep 2: `FamilyOfElements.singletonEquiv._proof_3` (`e85d215`)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Leftover | `CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.singletonEquiv._proof_3` |
| Decl# | `#211662` on the Mathlib aggregator |
| Error class | `REJECT` application argument type mismatch |

Not HasSize. Not intern-reset large-elim (814KB decl-closure slice rejects the same way). Measurement-skip of `*instRxiHasSize_eq*` / `*instRxcHasSize_eq*` was not needed: checking from decl 1, intern resets, those theorems did not fire before this leftover.

### Dump (`KIOTA_DEBUG`, slice)

`Eq.trans` argument: `eq_self` of `x proof_1`.

```
got:      Eq (Eq (P.obj (op X)) (x proof_1) (x proof_1)) True
expected: Eq (Eq (P.obj (op X)) (x proof_1) (x singleton.mk)) True
```

`_proof_1` is `Eq.rec trivial` along `singleton f f = True`. `singleton.mk` is the ctor. Both inhabit `singleton f f : Prop`. Innermost NEQ: those two proofs, then `x proof_1` vs `x singleton.mk` (bvar spine, pairwise).

`obviously_not_proof(singleton.mk)` was true because `inductive singleton : Presieve X` and `def Presieve X := ∀ Y, (Y ⟶ X) → Prop` peels to a def app, not `Sort 0`. PI never ran.

### Fix

Skip PI on a constructor only when the inductive's declared kind is a **non-zero Sort** (`… → Sort u` with `u ≠ 0`). A def-codomain Prop family is not “obviously data”. `Nat.zero` stays skipped. `True` ≢ `False` unchanged.

Unit test: `def_codomain_prop_ctor_converts_by_pi` (`def Pred := True → Prop`, `inductive One : Pred`).

Slice after the fix: **ACCEPT**.

---

title: Harden kernel soundness, completeness, and large-corpus stability
body:
Single release-candidate PR for the Kiota checker. Supersedes #1, #4, #6, and #7.

### What lands

- Rejects self-reference, orphan/misnamed recursors and constructors, and illegal `Prop` large elimination.
- Validates numeral shortcuts and reconstructs recursor/iota facts instead of trusting exported metadata.
- Closes Acc, projection, nested-recursion, constructor-universe, and defeq gaps found across Arena, Init/Std, Cedar, and focused mathlib slices.
- Removes declaration-name proof shortcuts; theorem values keep full argument checking.
- Bounds pathological `Nat.rec` and interner growth, clears generation-sensitive caches before an interner reset, and drops deep expression spines iteratively.
- Keeps `CONV_DEPTH=8192`; `KIOTA_NBE=1` remains optional and verdict-compatible.

### Verification

Head `5685c00`: 81 lib + 68 export tests pass under both default and `KIOTA_NBE=1`; CI and `git diff --check` pass. Latest Arena sweep on this line: 0 false accepts / 0 false rejects / 0 declines.

### AI/LLM disclosure

AI coding tools assisted with code and text. I reviewed the complete change and ran the reported tests.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes kernel acceptance rules (constructor/recursor metadata, nested inductive reconstruction) and optional defeq via NbE; incorrect validation or intern-table reset could cause false accepts or unsound comparisons.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`bench.sh`** to compare default eager checking vs **`KIOTA_NBE=1`** on an ndjson prefix, reporting valgrind callgrind **`Ir`** (and optional **`perf`** instructions) as JSON with repeat determinism flags.
> 
> **Expression interning** gets an iterative **`Drop`** for deep **`App`** spines (avoids stack overflow on teardown) and **`intern_clear_if_large`**, which can reset the hash-cons table past a threshold—callers must clear pointer-keyed caches first (documented in **`expr.rs`**). **`KIOTA_STATS`** now also prints **`intern_calls`** and **`live_nodes`**.
> 
> Introduces **`src/nbe`** as an optional NbE spike: **`KIOTA_NBE`** is parsed so only **`1`/`true`/`yes`** enable NbE (**`0`** no longer accidentally turns it on). The module defines **`Value`**, **`Neutral`**, and memoizing **`Thunk`**; full **`eval`** / **`is_def_eq`** routing lives in **`tc.rs`** (not in this diff slice).
> 
> **Inductive block parsing** is tightened: constructors must match their owner's declared **`ctors`** list; recursors need non-empty **`all`** with declared inductives and names matching **`I.rec`** / **`I.rec_N`**. **Nested specialization counting** fixes **`ctor_field_tys`** by shifting each field domain to a common binder depth, and **`note_nested_app`** deduplicates nested types by structural **`Expr`** equality instead of **`Rc`** addresses—addressing non-terminating BFS on shapes like deep **`List`** / **`Entry`** nests.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 5685c00d86065b1766aff7361edee1010d66d9b9. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

title: Reset unfold and iota memos before dropping the intern table
body: Onto PR #2 (`d1677c2`). Does not raise `CONV_DEPTH`. Pin stays held. `c54935a` dropped the intern table past 4M nodes, which is why the 621 MB prefix now finishes under 1.5 GB. Two leftovers in that reset: **Order.** `intern_clear_if_large` ran *between* the pointer-keyed WHNF/defeq/infer clears and the four `eager_*` twins. That window is comments today, so nothing can reuse a freed address before those maps go — but the invariant is only accidentally true. Eager caches now clear first, then the intern drop. **What still pinned the old generation.** `unfold_cache` is keyed by `(name, levels)` and was deliberately kept across declarations. After an intern drop its entries hold strong `Rc`s to pre-clear bodies while everything newly interned is a post-clear copy: `ptr_eq` and the pointer-keyed defeq cache miss on exactly the largest terms. `iota_lit_memo` keys on raw `usize` addresses of motives and minors, so a recycled address is a wrong hit. `iota_value_cache` holds `Rc`s into the same terms and would keep them alive anyway. Those three now drop in the same reset, and only when intern is actually past 4M, so Init/Std keep the unfold memo. `KIOTA_INTERN_RESET_LOG` prints intern and unfold sizes either side of a firing. 81 lib + 68 export green, unset and `KIOTA_NBE=1`. 186 tarball tests: 0/0/0 in 6.2 s. `lean-doc-block-nested-rec-param-shift` and `cedar-prefix-60` still accept. ### AI/LLM disclosure - AI coding tools were used to help draft or modify this code and PR description. - The complete change was reviewed and the reported tests were run before submitting. - This submission is original work of authorship under the project CLA / contributor terms; AI output was not pasted unreviewed.

title: Set up Cloud Agent dev environment + fix deep-spine Drop stack overflow
body: ## Summary Sets up and validates the Cloud Agent development environment for `kiota` (a from-scratch Lean 4 kernel checker in Rust) and fixes a latent stack-overflow crash surfaced while validating the test suite. The environment itself is minimal: the Cursor default image already ships the pinned Rust toolchain (`cargo`/`rustc` 1.83.0), so the only repository bootstrap needed is `cargo build --release` (which also warms the dependency cache). No dev server, database, or secrets are required — `kiota` is a CLI that reads an exported Lean environment and returns an accept/reject/decline verdict via exit code. ## The bug this uncovered While repeatedly running `cargo test` (the CI command in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`), the lib test binary intermittently crashed with `SIGSEGV` (~1 in 3 runs). Root cause: `intern_primary_reuses_after_many_unique` builds an ~8000-deep left-nested `App` chain, and `Expr = Rc` had no custom `Drop`. The compiler-derived recursive drop walks one stack frame per spine node, overflowing the small libtest thread stack during teardown. This is a genuine robustness defect — the checker could `SIGSEGV` instead of returning a verdict on deeply-nested terms. ### Fix Add an iterative `Drop for ExprNode` (`src/expr.rs`) that dismantles owned children with a heap worklist, so teardown depth is O(1) regardless of term depth. Confirmed with a large `RUST_MIN_STACK` that the crash was a stack overflow, then verified the fix holds at the default stack. ## Validation | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | `cargo test` (CI command) | 67 lib + 36 integration tests pass; 10/10 full runs clean (was ~1/3 SIGSEGV before) | | `cargo test --lib` stress | 20/20 clean at default stack | | `cargo build --release` | Succeeds; produces `target/release/kiota` | | Binary: valid export | ACCEPT, exit `0` | | Binary: `--use-stdin` valid export | ACCEPT, exit `0` | | Binary: invalid exports | REJECT, exit `1`, with diagnostic message | | Environment build (install = `cargo build --release`) | SUCCEEDED (fresh checkout + install, exit 0) | ## Notes - Scope is intentionally minimal (one 38-line addition to `src/expr.rs`). Pre-existing `rustfmt` diffs in `src/tc.rs` and existing compiler warnings are left untouched (CI runs only `cargo test`, not `fmt`). - The environment install command (`cargo build --release`) is proposed via the Cloud Agent environment panel for the user to Save.

title: Definition can reference itself while its body is being checked
body:
## Summary

Kiota accepts a hand-crafted export containing an ordinary definition equivalent to:

```lean
def cutoffSelf : Sort 1 := cutoffSelf
```

The official Lean kernel rejects it because `cutoffSelf` is not available while its own body is being checked. Lean4Lean and Nanoda also reject the witness. A matched control whose body is `Sort 0` is accepted by all four checkers.

This report concerns only acceptance of this malformed declaration class; it does not make a broader claim about Kiota.

## Reproducer

Reproduced against Kiota `main` at `686063c13b22ce379c05dfe7fc03656655ac60e5` after a clean release build.

Save this as `cutoff-self.ndjson`:

```ndjson
{"meta":{"exporter":{"name":"lean4export","version":"3.1.0"},"format":{"version":"3.1.0"},"lean":{"githash":"f72c35b3f637c8c6571d353742168ab66cc22c00","version":"4.29.1"}}}
{"in":1,"str":{"pre":0,"str":"cutoffSelf"}}
{"il":1,"succ":0}
{"ie":0,"sort":1}
{"const":{"name":1,"us":[]},"ie":1}
{"def":{"all":[1],"hints":"opaque","levelParams":[],"name":1,"safety":"safe","type":0,"value":1}}
```

Then run:

```console
cargo build --release
target/release/kiota cutoff-self.ndjson
echo $?
```

Observed Kiota result: exit `0` (`ACCEPT`).

Observed official Lean 4.33 result: exit `1` (`REJECT`):

```text
while replaying declaration 'cutoffSelf':
(kernel) unknown constant 'cutoffSelf'
```

## Positive control

The control uses a distinct name and replaces the self-reference expression with `{"ie":1,"sort":0}`. Its final declaration still has `"type":0,"value":1`. Both Kiota and the official checker accept it, so the disagreement is specific to visibility of the declaration under validation rather than general file construction.

## Suspected mechanism

`handle_def_like` inserts the definition into `self.env`, then `handle_line` calls `check_last`. `check_last` constructs a checker over that environment, and `check_decl` retrieves the already-inserted declaration and validates its value in the same environment. The current declaration can consequently resolve itself while its body is inferred.

Relevant code:

- [`handle_def_like`](https://github.com/sankalpsthakur/kiota/blob/686063c13b22ce379c05dfe7fc03656655ac60e5/src/parser.rs#L248-L299)
- [definition parsing followed by `check_last`](https://github.com/sankalpsthakur/kiota/blob/686063c13b22ce379c05dfe7fc03656655ac60e5/src/parser.rs#L785-L787)
- [`check_last` constructs the checker from `self.env`](https://github.com/sankalpsthakur/kiota/blob/686063c13b22ce379c05dfe7fc03656655ac60e5/src/parser.rs#L823-L885)

## Recorded evidence

- [Investigation report](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/829c72e/docs/investigations/NANODA_ENV_CUTOFF_SURVIVOR.md)
- [Machine-readable upstream-main reproduction](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/829c72e/results/investigations/kiota-self-reference/upstream-main.json)
- [Witness](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/829c72e/corpus/generated/nanoda-gen-8317efea2c7d-self-reference.ndjson) and [positive control](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/829c72e/corpus/generated/nanoda-gen-8317efea2c7d-self-reference-control.ndjson)

title: Arena verdict fixes — now mostly superseded by PR #2, except elim_only_at_universe_zero
body: ## Status: do not merge as-is PR #2 has independently landed equivalents of nearly everything here, including the two pieces cherry-picked from this branch (`dd63930`: the `I.rec` name gate and the `declaring` hide). Both branches now measure **0 false accepts / 0 false rejects / 0 declines** over the 193 arena tarball tests, on the same box: | branch | false accepts | false rejects | declines | wall (193 tests) | |---|---|---|---|---| | arena pin `58e8636` | 6 | 5 | 1 | — | | PR #2 tip `d11c4e0` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 7.2 s | | this branch `a62e7d2` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 7.0 s | **The one thing here that PR #2 does not have is `elim_only_at_universe_zero`.** That should be ported across; the rest of this branch should be closed. ## Why the large-elimination rule matters PR #2 gates its check on `all.len() == 1 && num_motives == 1` and `ctors.len() >= 2`, and its own comment notes "Mutual/multi-motive recursors are left unvalidated here". Lean's `elim_only_at_universe_zero` (`src/kernel/inductive.cpp`) forbids large elimination in three cases, not one: 1. `is_not_zero(result_level)` is false and the group has **more than one type** — mutual `Prop` groups eliminate only into `Prop`. 2. More than one constructor. *(This is the only case PR #2 covers.)* 3. Exactly one constructor, where some non-parameter field is **neither a proof nor exposed in the conclusion**. Case 3 is a live `False` route and is now pinned as `tests/fixtures/single-ctor-prop-large-elim.reject.ndjson`: ``` inductive Bad : Prop | mk (x : Sort 1) Bad.rec.{u} : (motive : Bad → Sort u) → ((x : Sort 1) → motive (Bad.mk x)) → (t : Bad) → motive t pick : Bad → Sort 1 := fun b => Bad.rec.{2} (fun _ => Sort 1) (fun x => x) b ``` One constructor, so the `ctors.len() >= 2` gate skips it. The field is data and `Bad`'s conclusion takes no arguments, so Lean fixes the motive at `Sort 0`. Measured: **PR #2 `d11c4e0` accepts this**, this branch rejects it at the recursor with "recursor of a Prop eliminates into a larger universe than Prop". `pick` pulls a type back out of a proof; proof irrelevance equates `Bad.mk A` with `Bad.mk B` for any two types while `pick` tells them apart — `large-elim-prop-bool` without the second constructor. ## What to port `elim_only_at_universe_zero`, `ctor_is_subsingleton` and `recursor_motive_level` in `src/tc.rs`, called from the end of `check_inductive_group` where the per-type result sorts are already computed. It follows the kernel's version clause for clause, including `is_not_zero` on the result level so `PUnit.{u}` and other `Sort u` inductives are unaffected, and the "field occurs in the conclusion" clause that keeps large elimination for single-constructor types carrying their data in indices. ## What not to port - **The `CONV_DEPTH` raise (`d936a2a`)** — rejected, and unnecessary: PR #2 accepts `church-numerals` in 8 ms at 8192. - The remaining commits — PR #2 has its own equivalents for the opaque reducibility hint, the `is_prop` universe instantiation, the projection rule, `selfProof` and `orphan-ctor`, all agreeing on every tarball verdict. ### AI/LLM disclosure - AI coding tools were used to help draft or modify this code and PR description. - The complete change was reviewed and the reported tests were run before submitting. - This submission is original work of authorship under the project CLA / contributor terms; AI output was not pasted unreviewed.

title: Universe-parameter ownership disagreement with official Lean
body:
## Summary

Kiota accepts a small Lean export containing a definition whose value references
universe parameter `u`, even though that definition declares no universe
parameters. The official Lean 4.33.0 kernel rejects the same artifact with
`defnInfo invalid`. Both checkers accept a positive control that declares `u` on
the definition.

This reproduces on current Kiota `main`, revision
`686063c13b22ce379c05dfe7fc03656655ac60e5`.

I am reporting this as a validator-behavior clarification and possible
correctness issue, not as a security vulnerability. Kiota is explicitly
experimental, and the evidence below establishes only this concrete
disagreement.

## Outcomes

| Input | Official Lean 4.33.0 | Kiota `686063c` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Undeclared-universe artifact | `REJECT` (exit 1) | `ACCEPT` (exit 0) |
| Declared-universe control | `ACCEPT` (exit 0) | `ACCEPT` (exit 0) |

The final declaration in the rejected artifact is conceptually:

```text
axiom unused.{u} : Prop
def bad : Prop := unused.{u}  // bad declares no universe parameters
```

## Minimal reproducer

- [Undeclared-universe artifact](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/2369a10e0aa57bf70499eee77d859fa44338f8d9/corpus/minimized/nanoda-0003-auto-universe-min.ndjson), SHA-256 `6743315bd44cd3ada0eb4a23336f73eca909ecbb6202c3fff3a8068bf0df101a`
- [Declared-universe control](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/2369a10e0aa57bf70499eee77d859fa44338f8d9/corpus/controls/nanoda-0003-declared-const-universe.ndjson), SHA-256 `94530b9892930781b8f91bb8eb5017e444ef564084ed2b6cfd3ce0eb858faab9`

```sh
git clone https://github.com/sankalpsthakur/kiota.git /tmp/kiota
git -C /tmp/kiota checkout 686063c13b22ce379c05dfe7fc03656655ac60e5
cargo build --release --manifest-path /tmp/kiota/Cargo.toml

curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/2369a10e0aa57bf70499eee77d859fa44338f8d9/corpus/minimized/nanoda-0003-auto-universe-min.ndjson -o /tmp/undeclared.ndjson
curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/2369a10e0aa57bf70499eee77d859fa44338f8d9/corpus/controls/nanoda-0003-declared-const-universe.ndjson -o /tmp/declared.ndjson

/tmp/kiota/target/release/kiota /tmp/undeclared.ndjson
echo $?  # 0 (ACCEPT)
/tmp/kiota/target/release/kiota /tmp/declared.ndjson
echo $?  # 0 (ACCEPT)
```

The complete four-outcome machine record is
[here](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/2369a10e0aa57bf70499eee77d859fa44338f8d9/results/investigations/kiota-universe-ownership/upstream-main.json).

## Question and possible validation point

Should Kiota require every universe parameter occurring in a declaration's type
or value to belong to that declaration's `levelParams` list? If so, could Kiota
reject the undeclared artifact and retain the declared artifact as a positive
control?

As a source-level hypothesis only, the current `Checker::check_decl` path appears
to check duplicate declared level parameters before type/value checking, but I
did not find a traversal enforcing ownership of every occurring universe
parameter. The relevant code is
[`src/tc.rs` lines 1394-1436](https://github.com/sankalpsthakur/kiota/blob/686063c13b22ce379c05dfe7fc03656655ac60e5/src/tc.rs#L1394-L1436).

The full investigation, validator identities, and explicit non-claims are in
the [Lean Assurance Lab report](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/2369a10e0aa57bf70499eee77d859fa44338f8d9/docs/investigations/KIOTA_UNIVERSE_OWNERSHIP.md).

This report does not claim arbitrary false propositions can be proved through
Kiota or general Kiota unsoundness beyond this malformed declaration class.

title: Harden kernel soundness, completeness, and large-corpus stability
body:
Single release-candidate PR for the Kiota checker. Supersedes #4, #6, and #7; benchmark-only #1 stays out of the kernel merge.

### What lands

- Rejects self-reference, orphan/misnamed recursors and constructors, and illegal `Prop` large elimination.
- Validates numeral shortcuts and reconstructs recursor/iota facts instead of trusting exported metadata.
- Closes Acc, projection, nested-recursion, constructor-universe, and defeq gaps found across Arena, Init/Std, Cedar, and focused mathlib slices.
- Removes declaration-name proof shortcuts; theorem values keep full argument checking.
- Bounds pathological `Nat.rec` and interner growth, clears generation-sensitive caches before an interner reset, and drops deep expression spines iteratively.
- Keeps `CONV_DEPTH=8192`; `KIOTA_NBE=1` remains optional and verdict-compatible.

### Verification

Combined head `5685c00`:

- default: 81 lib + 68 export tests pass
- `KIOTA_NBE=1`: 81 lib + 68 export tests pass
- `git diff --check`: pass
- latest Arena sweeps on this line: 0 false accepts / 0 false rejects / 0 declines

After squash-merge, Arena should pin the resulting `main` SHA.

title: Add scripts/bench.sh measurement harness (instructions/wall/RSS, no perf)
body: ## What Adds a small, narrow measurement harness so we can A/B instruction counts without Linux `perf`: - `scripts/bench.sh [--prefix N]` - Builds `--release` from a git SHA if needed (cached per-SHA under `.bench-cache//` via `git worktree`, so repeat runs against the same SHA don't rebuild), or uses an already-built binary path directly. - Runs under `valgrind --tool=callgrind` for instruction counts when `valgrind` is on `PATH`; otherwise prints a clear skip notice on stderr and reports `instructions: null`. - Measures `wall_ms` / `peak_rss_kb` from a separate, unaltered (no-valgrind) run, since valgrind's overhead makes its own timing/RSS numbers meaningless for comparison. - Emits one JSON object: `instructions`, `wall_ms`, `peak_rss_kb`, `sha`, `prefix`. - `--prefix N` sets the **existing** `KIOTA_MAX_DECL` env var (already read in `src/parser.rs`) to bound how many declarations are processed, for repeatable A/B runs on a fixed-size prefix of a large corpus. - `scripts/README-bench.md` documents usage, including how to run the harness twice on the same SHA to sanity-check run-to-run variance before trusting a cross-SHA comparison. No URLs required. - `README.md` gets a one-line pointer to the new docs. - `.gitignore` ignores `.bench-cache/`. ## What this does NOT do - No changes to WHNF, substitution, or any soundness-relevant checking code (`src/tc.rs`, `src/expr.rs`, `src/nat.rs`, `src/parser.rs` checking logic, etc. are untouched — verified via `git diff --stat` showing only `README.md`, `.gitignore`, and new files under `scripts/`). - No new env var was added to the kernel; the script reuses `KIOTA_MAX_DECL`, which already existed in `src/parser.rs`. ## Testing - `bash -n scripts/bench.sh` passes. - Ran locally against a built `./target/release/kiota` binary and against `HEAD` (via the git-worktree build path), with and without `--prefix`, confirming valid JSON output, cached-build reuse on a second run, and a graceful skip message when `valgrind`/`/usr/bin/time` aren't installed (as in this sandbox).
